07.name: July
beats: Days 1–5 — Empires fall on paper before they fall in history. Daniel 8–12 seals the end; Jeremiah’s nations scroll ends with Babylon’s doom; Isaiah mocks the gods that cannot carry their own statues. You watched heaven write the score while earth still thought it was the referee.

Days 6–19 — Ezekiel entire. Throne-chariot. Watchman. Glory departing. Bad shepherds / true Shepherd. Dry bones. Temple river. Parallel: Ezra’s lists, opposition, temple finished, Ezra’s arrival. Rebuild is holiness with a census roll, not bricks alone.

Days 15–27 — Nehemiah’s wall and the Word. Cupbearer to builder. Sword and trowel. Torah read until weeping, then feast. Covenant sealed. Minors preach beside the wall: Joel, Amos, Jonah, Micah, Nahum.

Days 28–31 — Esther opens; Haggai and Zechariah ignite. “For such a time as this.” Habakkuk’s faith, Zephaniah’s day, Haggai’s house, Zechariah’s night visions. God rules trowel and throne room on the same page.

Peace track — Isaiah’s burden, then Hosea’s heart, then comfort. You closed many nights not with a soft psalm but with judgment oracles that still end in hope. That is July’s tone: hard truth, stubborn mercy.

ahead.title: July 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: July will not babysit you. It will take you from the last visions of a captive prophet to a sleepless Persian king — through Ezekiel, return and rebuild, the minor prophets, and the quiet courage of a Jewish queen. You will start in Babylon’s shadow. You will finish with a hammer in one hand and a decree of death hanging over a people God will not abandon.
ahead.charge: Enter July awake. Empires will fall on the page before they fall in history. Keep the five watches. When dry bones rattle, do not rush past the Word that raises them.

review.title: July 2026 · Month in Review
review.lede: July did not babysit you. It took you from the last visions of a captive prophet to a sleepless Persian king — through the full weight of Ezekiel, the grit of return and rebuild, the thunder of the minor prophets, and the quiet courage of a Jewish queen. You started in Babylon’s shadow. You finished with a hammer in one hand and a decree of death hanging over a people God would not abandon.
review.charge: Do not leave July as a finished checklist. Leave it as a man who has seen empires judged, a temple measured, a wall finished, and a queen step into risk because silence would have been sin. Carry that into August — the Old Testament is about to close its mouth, and the Word is about to become flesh on the page in front of you.

08.name: August
chips: Gospels written later · W c. AD 50–90
beats: Days 1–3 — OT last words. Esther’s climax and Purim. Zechariah’s pierced one and fountain. Malachi’s messenger, refiner, and sun of righteousness. Then the page turns: two genealogies. The silence after Malachi is not empty — it is pregnant.
Days 4–9 — Incarnation and early signs. Annunciation. Nativity. Baptism under Tiberius. Temptation. Cana. Nicodemus. Samaritan woman. Nazareth’s rejection. The kingdom enters as a Person.

Days 10–22 — Galilee authority and rising cost. Demons silenced. Paralytic forgiven. Twelve sent. Sabbath conflict. Lord’s Prayer. Lost sheep/coin/ prodigal . The Son of Man already walks toward a cross while He heals on the way.

Days 23–29 — Holy Week compressed. Tears over Jerusalem. Entry. Temple cleanse. Olivet. Virgins, talents, sheep and goats. Chronological, not liturgical — the King rides in while the calendar still says late summer.

Days 30–31 — Upper Room threshold. Plot. Passover prep. Anointing at Bethany. Betrayal priced. Foot washing. “I am the way.” You will not finish the Passion in August — you will be positioned inside it, towel and table and night, ready for September to continue.

ahead.title: August 2026 · Month Ahead
ahead.lede: August is a hinge month. In three days the Old Testament closes its mouth. By the end of the first week the Word has become flesh on the page — birth, baptism, temptation, Cana. By the last week you are already in Passion week, washing feet and hearing “I am the way.” You will start with a gallows prepared for Mordecai. You will finish in an upper room with a towel around the Lord’s waist.
ahead.charge: Enter August awake. The prophets have done their shouting. The genealogies are about to name a Man. Keep the five watches. Keep the dual clocks. When the week turns holy before the month ends, do not rush past the tears over Jerusalem to get to the next checkbox. He is riding toward a cross — and you are riding with the text.

review.title: August 2026 · Month in Review
review.lede: August was a hinge month. In three days the Old Testament closed its mouth. By the end of the first week the Word had become flesh on the page — birth, baptism, temptation, Cana. By the last week you were already in Passion week, washing feet and hearing “I am the way.” You started with a gallows prepared for Mordecai. You finished in an upper room with a towel around the Lord’s waist.
review.charge: Do not leave August as a finished checklist. Leave it as a man who met a King on the page. Carry the dual clocks and the towel-and-table posture into September.
